llm.summary: This is mostly a coherent teacher report helper, but it should be reviewed because it handles sensitive student records and includes some under-scoped record-management and locale-specific crisis guidance.

dimensions.detail: The skill's read access to longitudinal student learning records is proportionate for report generation, but its crisis resources are framed around Mainland China emergency numbers without a locale gate, which can be unsafe outside that region.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact is a self-contained Markdown skill package with references and shared Markdown files; I found no executable install scripts, network fetches, credential collection, or hidden runtime setup.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Some activation examples are broad and do not consistently require a target student or explicit confirmation before workspace records are read, which is risky for sensitive student data.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The main interface says the skill writes only confirmed progressEvidence, but a renewal script also instructs changing studentCards[].status and handling retention/deletion, expanding mutation authority beyond the declared write scope.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is to generate staged learning reports and renewal wording from existing lesson, homework, progress, package, consent, and parent-communication records; that data use is disclosed and largely purpose-aligned.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if this will be used in a Chinese-language teaching workspace where teachers explicitly select the student before generating a report. Before use, clarify that it may read sensitive student learning records, require consent before any parent-facing output, keep message sending manual, and constrain any student status changes or deletion requests to your platform's governed record-management process. Do not rely on the included crisis hotline wording outside Mainland China without local emergency guidance.
llm.findings:
[AE1] expected: Downgraded: shared/vocab.md is present in the artifact and was inspected; references to a shared vocabulary file are normal for this package and do not show analysis evasion.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Accepted as a scope concern: broad phrases such as generic renewal or parent-question prompts could trigger sensitive student-record processing without a clearly required student identifier or confirmation step.
[SQP-3] expected: Mostly downgraded for the Chinese-language script and vocabulary files: the skill name, author, audience, and content clearly target Chinese-speaking independent teachers, so Chinese output is coherent with purpose.
[SQP-3] unexpected: Accepted for crisis guidance: shared crisis files provide Mainland China-specific emergency and hotline numbers as defaults without requiring locale detection or a neutral fallback first.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted as a material under-disclosure issue: references/renewal-communication-scripts.md instructs changing studentCards[].status after course ending, while SKILL.md declares progressEvidence[] as the only direct write target.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted as a data-governance concern: retention and deletion timing appears inside a renewal communication script and says to execute early deletion on parent request, while confirmation and authorization boundaries are not fully specified there.
